newsitem.title: USA: Conrail deal criticized by labor leaders.
newsitem.headline: Conrail deal criticized by labor leaders.

text.p: Labor officials criticized a pending Conrail merger at a state public hearing on Thursday, contending that such a transaction would hurt the railroad's workers and stunt competition.

"While a few might benefit from a war of capital, it is easy to conclude that Conrail's employees will be the ultimate losers as jobs are slashed and job security evaporates," said Sam Nasca, state director of the United Transportation Union.
Nasca spoke at the first of three hearings to be conducted by the New York Department of Transportation.

Philadelphia-based Conrail, which operates on 2,000 miles of track in New York, is negotiating a transaction to be acquired by CSX Corp for $10.3 billion, or $115 per share. Conrail, which has an existing pact with CSX, is seeking to revise the deal in order to match a rival bid from Norfolk Southern Corp. That would set the stage for a division of Conrail's assets between CSX and Norfolk.

Nasca was one of nine speakers at the hearing, which was attended by more than 50 people, including railroad officials and shippers. He said railroad unions were urging the three companies to let them review any acquisition plans.

The New York Transportation Department is conducting the hearings in order to make recommendations to the U.S. Surface Transportation Board, the federal regulator responsible for the final approval of any rail merger in the United States.

Representatives of Conrail and CSX did not attend the hearing. Meanwhile, Norfolk Southern expressed its eagerness to expand in New York, where it now operates a 100-mile track out of Buffalo toward Cleveland and Chicago.
"We feel the resolution will be favorable, but it is tenuous at this time," said James Granum, Norfolk Southern's vice president for public affairs.

Representatives from Canadian Pacific/Delaware & Hudson and New England-based Gilford Railroad, both of which presently rent many of their tracks from Conrail in New York, said they looked forward to having a chance to own tracks and want to be considered in any state negotiations.
The department will hold a hearing on Friday in Buffalo and another meeting on March 13 in Manhattan.
